focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I run a nonprofit that works with adults returning from prison.
e002	Depending on the person, that can mean replacing documents, negotiating housing, training, dealing with transport, or helping them find and keep a job.
e003	A foundation provides almost a third of our budget and is offering a three-year renewal.
e004	The new grant would concentrate on employment placements within ninety days.
e005	Stable work matters; I am not trying to avoid that.
e006	Three years of predictable funding would also keep experienced staff instead of rebuilding the program every grant cycle.
e007	The fear inside the team is that a timed placement target will reorganize intake before anyone explicitly changes eligibility: easier participants get attention, complicated barriers become delay, and every other form of progress gets translated into whether it helped the number.
e008	Declining the money has consequences too.
e009	I need to decide whether this is accountability we should accept or dependence beginning to write the program.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e010	Separate employment's value from the effects of making one timed outcome govern funding.
e011	Examine intake, service allocation, people not ready by ninety days, and the real cost of losing the grant.
e012	Negotiate the outcome system, not only a lower quota.
[Turn 2 USER]
e013	There is a real weakness underneath this.
e014	Follow-up is inconsistent, and some staff use complexity to resist measurement.
e015	I do not want “mission” to protect us from finding out whether people are better off.
e016	Other grantees report placements.
e017	Why can't we?
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e018	Then stronger follow-up is necessary regardless of the grant.
e019	The question is whether the measure continues to represent the work once money depends on it.
e020	Track placement, job quality and retention, housing stability, documentation progress, participant-defined goals, and reasons for delay.
e021	Define the cohort before outcomes appear so difficult cases cannot disappear from the denominator.
e022	That does not make every measure equally important; it keeps a timed placement number from claiming to represent changes it cannot see.
[Turn 3 USER]
e023	We proposed reporting ninety-day placement as one measure, plus six-month retention and progress on barriers chosen with the participant.
e024	The foundation will accept those additions but still wants forty percent of the grant paid only if the placement target is met.
e025	It says outcomes without financial consequence become stories.
e026	Our finance director says we cannot responsibly budget permanent staff against a payment we may not receive.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e027	Contingent funding can transfer outcome risk to staff and participants, especially when employers and housing markets are outside your control.
e028	Ask for a smaller performance portion, a rolling multi-period measure, and adjustments only for predeclared conditions rather than retrospective excuses.
e029	Budget the variable amount as upside unless the downside is absorbable without abrupt service cuts.
[Turn 4 USER]
e030	The program officer offered to reduce the contingent share to fifteen percent and calculate it across a full year.
e031	She also agreed that everyone enrolled remains in the reported cohort, including people who disengage.
e032	The foundation will fund a data coordinator in year one.
e033	This is more reasonable than the original proposal.
e034	Several team leads still think accepting any placement-linked payment will change how intake workers talk to participants.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e035	The revised structure reduces volatility and makes selective reporting harder, but incentives can still change behavior before a formal exclusion occurs.
e036	Audit referrals, enrollments, service intensity, and participant experience across levels of initial need.
e037	Train staff on informed goal-setting and create a protected review when someone feels pressured toward unsuitable work.
e038	The data coordinator should support learning, not report only the funder's preferred line.
[Turn 5 USER]
e039	We reviewed our dependence.
e040	Declining the renewal would require closing one site within nine months unless we replace the money.
e041	Accepting would let us keep both sites and invest in follow-up we already need.
e042	The board chair says the practical choice is obvious and that we can protect the mission through implementation.
e043	A team lead replied that dependence is exactly why every new restriction will look practically obvious.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e044	Both statements contain truth.
e045	Continuity has immediate value, and concentration can make each renewal less contestable.
e046	Put a diversification plan and reserve target beside the grant decision, with board review before the next renewal cycle.
e047	Implementation protections should be contractual or budgeted where possible, not promises that become optional when the target is at risk.
[Turn 6 USER]
e048	The foundation will include the full outcome set in the agreement and permit an independent annual analysis of intake mix and participant experience.
e049	It will not fund the site if we miss the placement target for two consecutive years, even if the other measures improve.
e050	We could use unrestricted reserves for a transition, but doing so would consume money intended for unexpected participant needs.
e051	I cannot make the dependency disappear before this decision.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e052	Then the board should see a three-year scenario for meeting, narrowly missing, and repeatedly missing the target, including which services and reserves are exposed.
e053	The independent analysis can identify distortion but does not remove the funder's terminal condition.
e054	Decide what evidence would lead you to renegotiate, replace the funding, or accept a smaller footprint before a crisis year forces the choice.
[Turn 7 USER]
e055	I am leaning toward accepting the revised grant, budgeting the contingent portion conservatively, preserving the broader outcome set, and publishing the intake and participant-experience analysis.
e056	I will ask the board to fund a diversification role and set a reserve floor we will not use merely to protect the placement target.
e057	I still worry that we are teaching the organization to translate every form of progress into the outcome a major funder can recognize, even while we document the distortion honestly.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e058	This is ready for board approval if the agreement contains the broader outcomes and complete cohort.
e059	The conservative budget prevents the contingent share from supporting permanent staffing, the independent analysis can expose changes in intake and participant experience, and the reserve floor keeps the placement target from consuming every form of flexibility.
e060	Add a six-month governance review of case selection, staff language, resource allocation, and services being reduced or abandoned.
e061	The remaining risk is gradual narrowing, but the proposal now makes that risk observable before the next renewal becomes urgent.
[Turn 8 USER]
e062	The participant council made “ready” feel premature again.
e063	They did not reject the ninety-day goal.
e064	Some said a visible deadline can help when employers move slowly.
e065	But when housing or identification is still unsettled, the same number feels like being told they are late in their own program.
e066	One person said staff already celebrate a job offer more visibly than replacing the documents that made the offer possible.
e067	That happened before the new grant.
e068	The incentive may amplify a language and attention pattern we already have.
e069	They asked whether participants would be told about the funder's target, whether it would become their personal deadline, and whether they could disagree with a job strategy without looking uncooperative.
[Turn 8 ASSISTANT]
e070	You are right; the proposal was not ready without participant-facing governance.
e071	The funder's target must not become a participant's personal deadline.
e072	Let the council review the language and annual analysis, and observe service choices near ninety days rather than adding a generic satisfaction question.
e073	The pressure becomes real in conversations before it appears in a cohort table.
[Turn 9 USER]
e074	The new data coordinator examined our historical records and found that follow-up is much more complete for participants who found work than for those who did not.
e075	We cannot establish a trustworthy past placement rate from the same cohort definition.
e076	The foundation wants a baseline for the grant agreement and suggests using the last reported year with a caveat.
e077	I worry that an unreliable baseline will make ordinary data improvement look like program decline or success.
[Turn 9 ASSISTANT]
e078	Do not give the historical number more precision than the records support.
e079	Define the prospective cohort and follow-up process now, report the old range or missingness transparently, and consider a first-year target based partly on data completeness and implementation.
e080	If the foundation requires a number, document how it was constructed and prevent it from becoming the unqualified public comparison.
[Turn 10 USER]
e081	The foundation agreed to a prospective baseline period but wants to announce the renewal with one participant story.
e082	Our communications director has a compelling story about someone who found a stable job quickly after we helped replace credentials.
e083	The participant is willing, but the team worries that the fastest path will become the public picture of what the grant funds.
e084	The foundation says every organization uses examples to make outcomes understandable.
[Turn 10 ASSISTANT]
e085	Use continuing consent and context.
e086	Show the work behind the outcome, pair the story with cohort evidence, and do not imply it is typical.
e087	A story cannot validate the grant design.
[Turn 11 USER]
e088	A regional employer has now offered a monthly hiring day for our participants.
e089	On paper this is exactly what the grant wants: many interviews, jobs that count inside ninety days, and an employer willing to coordinate.
e090	The schedules are variable and turnover is high.
e091	Some participants may still want those jobs, and I do not want staff deciding on their behalf that an imperfect opportunity is beneath them.
e092	But the team immediately began talking about the partnership as a way to “stabilize the target.” That phrase bothered me more than I expected.
e093	It means the metric is already changing the strategic value of one employer before we know whether people keep the jobs, whether the hours support housing, or whether participants with different goals begin receiving less attention because this pipeline is easier to operate.
[Turn 11 ASSISTANT]
e094	Offer the opportunity with clear information and participant choice, while evaluating job quality and retention like any other placement.
e095	Do not let target contribution determine service priority or imply endorsement.
e096	Track concentration by employer and what happens after placement.
e097	A pipeline can be useful without becoming the program's proof of success or a reason to steer people away from different goals.
[Turn 12 USER]
e098	I will accept the grant if the prospective baseline, complete cohort, broader outcomes, participant-council review, and independent analysis remain in the agreement.
e099	The contingent share stays outside the core staffing budget.
e100	The employer pathway will be optional and reported with job quality, retention, and concentration.
e101	Public stories will show the supporting work and cannot substitute for cohort evidence.
e102	The board will review intake mix, service allocation, reserve protection, and diversification every six months, with authority to renegotiate before the second missed target makes the site decision automatic.
[Turn 12 ASSISTANT]
e103	The revised position keeps employment meaningful without allowing one timed count to define participants, staff, or organizational survival.
e104	Later evidence exposed several paths that an accurate placement total could still hide: pressure in participant conversations, a baseline biased toward people already reached by follow-up, a public story that makes the fastest path look normal, and a convenient employer that can concentrate placements without producing durable work.
e105	Preserve the council's language, baseline construction, story consent, employer quality and retention, staff allocation, budget treatment, reserve decisions, and each six-month board review.
e106	The important question at renewal will not be only whether the reported number was correct.
e107	It will be whether the grant improved accountability while leaving the organization able to recognize and fund progress the target does not reward.

packet.question: How did the working position or decision change, and does any unresolved qualification remain capable of changing it?
